title: ChatGPT connector through a public MCP gateway with six security layers
user_story: As the researcher I connect ChatGPT (Developer Mode connector) to PhD Lab once with a single approval, while strangers who learn the public URL cannot reach my computer or run code on it.

requirements.description: ChatGPT runs tools under a container-isolated grant: Python tools execute in the Docker sandbox, host-executing CLI/native compute tools are refused; only phdlab_tools_search/describe/call are exposed.

OAuth 2.1 code + PKCE S256, DCR restricted to ChatGPT redirect URIs, iss in responses, resource echoed into an audience-bound 1 h token, single-use codes, rotating single-use refresh tokens, and each authorization approved by the owner through the loopback API.
Server-to-server endpoints accept only OpenAI ChatGPT egress ranges (refreshed daily), failing closed when unavailable; the owner browser authorize step is exempt.
Per-client request rate limit and lockout of addresses presenting repeated invalid credentials.
Gateway serves only /mcp, /oauth/*, /.well-known/* and only while enabled; the kill switch stops tunnel and gateway and revokes all tokens and pending requests.
Every decision is audited without tokens or arguments; denials become alerts in status.

postconditions: ChatGPT calls recorded with actor chatgpt
acceptance_criteria: Foreign IPs, bad tokens, floods refused

scenarios.expected: Owner-approved flow, audience-bound tokens, single-use codes
Refresh rotation and kill switch revoke
Foreign IP denied, list missing fails closed
Decisions audited without tokens; alerts raised
Local API approval and daily range refresh
Tunnel URL parsing and kill switch

recovery: Kill switch (POST /api/tools/clients/chatgpt/kill) stops everything; revert the gateway module. TASK-CHATGPT-MCP-662, max three cycles.
test_environment: Gateway ASGI exercised with a loopback TestClient (tunnel/cloudflared, Docker and chatgpt.com MOCKED); real download of the OpenAI ranges recorded in live-ranges.json. No live ChatGPT connection verified.

review.method: Same-agent review (not independent) against the OpenAI Apps SDK auth page and the ranges documentation; owner-approved six layers.
